wikiGoal: A code wiki for this repository.

pages.title: Controlled Assistant Agent Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the LangGraph-based controlled general agent, its layers, node graph, and evidence-domain routing.
instructions: Cover layer responsibilities, evidence-domain routing (direct/structured_data/private_document/public_current/mixed), DAG vs ReAct selection, and approval/resume.

Document the LangGraph node graph (context_resolver, goal_extractor, ambiguity_checker, planner, evaluators, capability matcher, DAG executor, ReAct loop, execution engine, approval, result processor).
Include a Mermaid diagram of the node flow and typical routes.
Note build_assistant_graph() uses AsyncPostgresSaver and requires a configured PostgreSQL database.url; the model must never be able to authorize its own side effects.

pages.title: CLI and Process Entrypoints
pages.purpose: Explain the Click CLI commands, backend process entry, base-dir/config resolution, and first-run behavior.
instructions: Cover the Click CLI (`bosshunter` → bosshunter.main:cli), `bosshunter-server` → bosshunter.backend:main, `--config` handling, base-dir resolution, first-run setup prompt, and Windows/start scripts.
Keep command behavior consistent with docs; note Python source uses tabs (ruff indent-style = tab) and line width 120.
List commands run/scrape/score/confirm/greet/send/monitor/resume/status/web/start/connect and their purpose without inventing behavior.

pages.title: System Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Provide a system map of owned systems, layer boundaries, entrypoints, and data flow so a coding agent can localize safe changes.
instructions: Document owned systems (job pipeline, AI generation, browser runtime, web dashboard, controlled assistant agent, infrastructure) and their boundaries rather than mirroring the source tree.
Include a top-level diagram of the scrape→score→confirm→send→monitor loop and the web/assistant layers.
Preserve safety rules from AGENTS.md: mandatory human confirmation, no auto-click of resume cards, single active background task, and browser runtime .mjs artifacts must ship with the wheel.

pages.title: Web Dashboard and Background Tasks
pages.purpose: Document the Bottle server, static React frontend, and the single-active-task workbench runner as one owned system.
instructions: Document the dashboard as an owned system: Bottle app serving /api/* plus dist/ static files, React pages (Dashboard, Config, AI Assistant), and WorkbenchTaskRunner.
Explain the single-active-task lock, cooperative stop event, deadline timer, task terminal states, and which modes are parallel-safe.
Preserve the rule: new web actions must respect the single-active-background-task constraint and must not spawn unbounded threads.

pages.title: Capability Registry and Approval Boundary
pages.purpose: Explain the capability registry as the authority for tool permissions, side effects, and the deterministic approval boundary.
instructions: Cover approval proposal lifecycle: persist, resume, re-validate, dispatch once, consume exactly once; the model cannot authorize itself.
Document CAPABILITY_REGISTRY fields (tool_name, risk_level, read_only, requires_approval, side_effect, tags, schemas) and the capability retriever/policy filtering.
Explain side-effect classes (none/local_reversible/local_persistent/external) and that user constraints such as '不要发送' must deterministically remove send capabilities.

pages.title: Job State Machine and Funnel
pages.purpose: Define job statuses, legal transitions, event records, and funnel metrics used across CLI, web, and assistant question answering.
instructions: Cover job_events and the PostgreSQL semantic views/trigger (semantic_job_current, semantic_job_funnel) and their metric definitions.
Document statuses (pending, scored, filtered, ready, approved, skipped, sent, replied, needs_resume, resume_sent, follow_up_sent, rejected, error) and legal transitions.
Include a Mermaid state diagram.
State explicitly that direct DB writes must not be used to skip human confirmation.

pages.title: Throttling, Send Windows, and Human Confirmation
pages.purpose: Document the rate limiting, send windows, daily limits, backoff, day-off logic, and mandatory confirmation that protect the external platform and the user.
instructions: Document RequestThrottle (Gaussian delay + burst penalty), PageThrottle, SendWindowChecker, ProgressiveBackoff, should_take_day_off, daily_limit, and browse-before-greet behavior.
Explain ui/confirm.py as the mandatory human confirmation point and its default-deny behavior.
State that default throttle values may only stay the same or become more conservative; never weaken confirmation, throttling, or platform safety checks.

pages.title: AI Provider Integration and Credentials
pages.purpose: Document AI provider dispatch, model resolution, retries, and secret handling across scorer, greeter, and resume generation.
instructions: Cover key resolution order (env then config) and the rule to not hardcode internal compatible-service names or domains.
Document anthropic and openai_compatible dispatch, base_url, /v1/models fuzzy matching and cache locking, request timeout clamping, and HTTP retry for 429/5xx plus network errors.
Note logs must not include API keys, full request headers, or unnecessary resume text; Web API must redact raw API keys; tests must mock AI boundaries.

pages.title: Web API Surface and Local Access
pages.purpose: Document the REST and SSE contract, local-access protection, upload/download safety, and streaming/cancel endpoints.
instructions: Cover loopback vs LAN binding, BOSSHUNTER_AUTH_TOKEN bearer auth, constant-time token comparison, and config redaction.

Document /api/* route groups: health, funnel/stats/activity, jobs, history, workbench, import, greetings/replies, assistant conversations/messages/stream/runs/resume/memories/bad-cases/ratings, config, resume, and avatar.
Document SSE stream pause/resume, run cancel, partial message persistence, and upload/download path-safety rules.
State that error responses must not leak credentials, resume text, or internal stack traces.

pages.title: Browser Runtime and CDP Automation
pages.purpose: Document the local Node CDP proxy, Python HTTP facade, browser launcher, and site-pattern maintenance.
instructions: Cover browser discovery/launch with an isolated user-data-dir profile and no stored platform credentials.
Document site patterns as the fragile selector boundary; selector fixes belong in scraper/executor with tests.
Document the Python HTTP facade (RuntimeClient) over the local Node CDP proxy, runtime auto-start, health/targets, port guard, fallback port switching, and RUNTIME_NOT_READY semantics.
State that browser/runtime/*.mjs and site-patterns/*.md are hatch artifacts that must ship with the wheel and must not be relocated.

pages.title: Configuration and Environment
pages.purpose: Document config.yaml defaults, merge semantics, Web schema, environment loading, and secret handling.
instructions: Cover .env loading via BOSSHUNTER_BASE_DIR and secret redaction rules; never commit config.yaml or real credentials.
Cover config.example.yaml as the canonical schema and web/config_schema.json as Web validation; new fields need defaults plus both schemas plus tests.

Document config domains (profile, search, scoring, throttle, ai, assistant, resume, monitor, follow_up, dedup, browser, database, runtime, artifacts), DEFAULTS deep-merge, provider validation, and city codes.

pages.title: Data Layer and Production Infrastructure
pages.purpose: Explain the unified database adapter, PostgreSQL migrations, Redis coordination, Dramatiq worker, and artifact store.
instructions: Cover Redis roles (session lock, cancel signal, event stream; never source of truth), Dramatiq registered tasks (send/pipeline tasks must not auto-retry), and local/S3 artifact stores with >16KB offload.
Document PostgreSQL as the production business DB (SQLite only for explicit local/test paths), the PostgresConnection adapter, and the four ordered migrations.
Document the RuntimeStore tables (agent_runs, agent_plan_steps, agent_observations, action_proposals, artifacts).
State that production components fail fast when unavailable; do not reintroduce silent in-process fallbacks.

pages.title: Release, Maintenance, and Governance
pages.purpose: Capture the Definition of Done, release checklist, feature freeze rules, maintenance priorities, and failure handling.
instructions: Document the Definition of Done, release checklist (wheel artifacts, redaction, data hygiene, doc/command consistency, frontend dist rebuild), feature freeze conditions, maintenance priorities, WIP limits, and P0-P3 failure grades.
Note frontend source changes require npm run build and committing the updated dist/.
State the license is LicenseRef-BossHunter-NonCommercial (not MIT) and ruff format indent-style is tab.

pages.title: Testing Strategy and Regression Coverage
pages.purpose: Document pytest layout, mocked boundaries, and the focused regression suites that protect fragile and safety-critical behavior.
instructions: Document pytest discovery (tests/test_*.py, pythonpath=src), ruff checks, and frontend `tsc`+Vite build with committed dist/.

Map major regression suites: web API routes, send retry, monitor reply detection/dismiss/navigation, resume PDF/templates, greeter quality/concurrency, scorer, job selection/enrichment, city codes, and assistant architecture/memory/evidence routing.
State that network, browser/CDP, and AI-provider boundaries must be mocked for determinism, and prefer the narrowest quiet validation with complete failure output.

pages.title: Assistant Question-Answer and Approval Flow
pages.purpose: Trace the assistant request lifecycle from message ingestion through LangGraph execution, streaming, approval, resume, and cancellation.
instructions: Cover cooperative cancellation (Redis cancel signal, partial messages not persisted as full answers) and checkpoint recovery.
Include a Mermaid sequence diagram.
State that external actions must re-validate the proposal and business state before dispatch and proposals must be consumed exactly once.
Trace send_message → session lock → graph.ainvoke → SSE token/ExecutionEvent streaming → persist result, and resume via Command(resume=decision) → action dispatcher.

pages.title: Job Hunt Pipeline (Scrape to Monitor)
pages.purpose: Trace the end-to-end ordered pipeline and where data, AI, browser, and human confirmation meet.
instructions: Cover stage failure handling, greeting-failure recovery back to approved, and where human confirmation gates sending.
Include a Mermaid sequence/flow diagram.
Note site selectors are fragile; scraper changes need regression tests.
Trace the ordered stages scrape→prefilter→score→confirm→greet→send→monitor and keep that ordering explicit.

pages.title: Sending, Reply Monitoring, and Follow-up
pages.purpose: Document greeting sending and HR reply monitoring, including resume-request classification and follow-up, with their safety boundaries.
instructions: Document send retry/recovery, progressive backoff, conversation navigation, HR reply candidate-vs-verified detection, resume-request card classification, single auto follow-up, and manual resume sending.
Include a Mermaid diagram of the send and monitor flows.
Note selector fixes belong in executor/ and require deterministic tests.
State that card detection only classifies and generates suggestions; it never auto-clicks agree/refuse/send and never sends without confirmation.

pages.title: BossHunter OpenWiki Quickstart
pages.purpose: Route readers into the wiki hierarchy and summarize the system and its non-negotiable safety boundaries before any code change.
instructions: Do not document config.yaml, data/, resumes, or credentials as source of truth.

Emphasize the invariants that must never be weakened: mandatory human confirmation, throttling/send windows, single active background task, and no auto-clicking agree/refuse/send on resume-request cards.
Route readers to /openwiki/architecture/overview.md first, then to workflow and operations pages based on the task.
State that this is BossHunter v2.0 (LicenseRef-BossHunter-NonCommercial, not MIT), Python 3.11+, with a React dashboard and a LangGraph assistant.
